headline: Messi builds football club empire, acquires Spanish second-tier club CD Eldense
summary: Lionel Messi is transitioning from player to club owner, recently acquiring Spanish second-tier club CD Eldense and focusing on youth development across Spain, Uruguay, and the US.
details: Lionel Messi is preparing for life after playing, shifting his focus from the pitch to club ownership. The 39-year-old football icon has made it clear that coaching doesn't appeal to him, but owning clubs does. This vision is rapidly becoming a reality, with operations spanning Spain, Uruguay, and eventually the United States.

Last week, Messi completed the acquisition of Spanish second-tier club CD Eldense, pending regulatory approval. This adds to his growing portfolio, which includes UE Cornella, a Catalan fifth-tier side he bought in April. These investments offer a glimpse into his post-playing career plans.

According to BBC Sport columnist Guillem Balague, Eldense is envisioned as the top-tier operation, while Cornella will primarily serve as a breeding ground for young talent. Messi, still active with Inter Miami, relies on trusted associates to manage the day-to-day operations of these Spanish clubs until he can dedicate more time.

Messi remains deeply involved, reportedly watching every Eldense match and celebrating their victories on Instagram. The takeover has significantly boosted Eldense's profile, attracting around a dozen potential sponsors within days, including brands already associated with Messi.

Despite his global reputation, Eldense's immediate ambition is modest: survival in Spain's Segunda Division. Former Villarreal coach Javi Calleja has been appointed, and Spanish financial rules limit the direct injection of funds into the playing squad.

His commitment to youth development extends beyond Spain. In Uruguay, he partnered with Luis Suarez in Deportivo LSM, a project focused on nurturing young talent that has already achieved promotion to the country's third tier. His Inter Miami contract also includes a future stake in the MLS club after his retirement.

Messi's involvement in youth football is further highlighted by the Messi Cup, an under-16 tournament launched in Miami. Starting with eight academies last year, it will double to 16 this month, featuring top clubs like Barcelona, Arsenal, and Chelsea, alongside his own Cornella.

"I don't see myself as a coach," Messi told Luzu TV. "I want to have my own club, start from the bottom and make it big. Being able to give kids the opportunity to develop and achieve something important." This philosophy underpins his expanding business interests in football.

headline_marked: [[Wives can demand outstanding dower immediately]], High Court rules, ending wait for divorce or death
headline: Wives can demand outstanding dower immediately, High Court rules, ending wait for divorce or death
summary: The High Court has ruled that husbands must immediately pay outstanding dower upon their wife's demand, eliminating the need to wait for divorce or the husband's death. This landmark decision clarifies a long-standing legal ambiguity.
details: Bangladesh's High Court has issued a historic ruling, stating that husbands must immediately pay any outstanding dower (denmohor) upon their wife's demand. Wives no longer have to wait for events like divorce or the husband's death to claim their dower.

Justice Abdur Rahman's single High Court bench delivered this groundbreaking observation and verdict while resolving a civil revision case concerning dower. The full judgment was officially published on the Supreme Court website on Tuesday.

The court observed that if a husband, despite having the financial means, unnecessarily delays or procrastinates dower payment and forces his wife to seek legal recourse, the relevant judicial court can order him to pay suitable compensation in addition to the original dower amount.

The High Court further clarified that no court has the legal authority to reduce, decrease, or waive any part of the dower under any circumstances. Such actions would constitute a clear violation of civil contracts and legal provisions.

Previously, while the existing Muslim Marriage and Divorce (Registration) Rules mentioned outstanding dower, there was no clear legal explanation regarding when it should be paid. This led to a common misconception that outstanding dower was only claimable after divorce or the husband's death.

This ruling resolves that long-standing legal ambiguity and backlog. The court referenced relevant verses from the Holy Quran, emphasizing that Islam does not allow dower to be delayed, considering it an immediate and inalienable right of the wife.

Barrister Ishrat Hasan, the lawyer involved in the case, hailed this verdict as a unique milestone in the country's legal arena and for the protection of women's rights. She stated that this ruling closes the door on women's long-standing deprivation in claiming outstanding dower.

With this judgment, husbands with financial capability can no longer procrastinate on dower payments. This verdict will stand as a significant precedent in the country's judicial history, ensuring women's social and financial security.
